Subject: Interim update — degraded inference success rates for Evergreen Bank

Hi Sara / Evergreen ops team,

Quick update from Redwood: since ~07:20 PDT we observed a degradation that caused higher-than-expected inference error rates for requests routed to the us-west region. Impact: a subset of Evergreen production requests returned 5xx or timeouts for short windows; latency spikes also observed.

What we know so far:
- Window: ~07:18–07:46 PDT; peak errors at ~07:26
- Visible impact: ~0.6% of total inference requests for EVB routing experienced errors; customers with pinned model variants experienced more retries
- Mitigation applied: we adjusted routing to a fallback-compatible model and increased autoscale headroom at 07:34, which restored normal success rates by 07:46

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Triage and root-cause investigation (engineering lead assigned)
2) Share a concise timeline + proposed corrective actions within 72 hours
3) Provide a verification plan you can run and we can run jointly

I know this disruption touched a small percentage of traffic but could affect sensitive flows. Apologies for the interruption — I’ll follow up with the detailed timeline and RCA as soon as the post-incident analysis completes.

If you want a short call to walk through the impact and our mitigation logs, I can set one up this afternoon.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Sara / Evergreen ops,

Attached is our post-incident summary and an initial verification plan for Evergreen. I’ll summarize the highlights here and call out owner commitments. PDF and timeline CSV attached for your records (shared folder link below).

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: a combination of a degraded kernel selection path in the serving runtime and an edge case in our routing policy that allowed a small percentage of requests to be routed to a partially-initialized worker pool. The partially-initialized pool returned errors during peak sequence lengths.
- Impact: 07:18–07:46 PDT, 2028-09-15 — ~0.6% error rate on EVB-routed traffic, peak at 07:26. No customer data was exposed; request payloads remained encrypted in transit.
- Mitigation: automated fallback to a verified model variant + increase in autoscale headroom at 07:34. Service restored by 07:46.

Key timeline (high level):
- 07:18: initial error patterns observed in metrics and customer alerts
- 07:22: SRE investigation — replication of errors with long-sequence request shapes
- 07:30: root-cause reproduction in staging — kernel selection + worker-init race discovered
- 07:34: temporary routing policy change and autoscale increase rolled to prod
- 07:46: observable success rates returned to baseline; monitoring continued for 2 hours

Action items and owners (short-term):
- Engineering (Aditya Rao): shipping patch to guard the kernel-selection path and add additional initialization checks (ETA: 2028-09-22)
- Runtime QA (Grace O'Connor): expanded regression tests for long-sequence inference shapes and a canary job for worker-init (ETA: 2028-09-24)
- Customer success (Kimberly Park / Marissa Cole): run joint verification and confirm expected behavior for Evergreen (plan below); coordinate credits discussion with finance/procurement (ETA: initial reply by 2028-09-21)

Verification plan (steps you can run with Redwood):
1) Shared synthetic test suite that mimics your long-sequence payloads (we will provide suite and sample inputs)
2) Run tests against a canary pool we control and a production-like pool in your region
3) Observe metrics for error rates and token-level latencies; Redwood will run parallel validation and share logs
4) Sign-off: two consecutive test runs with error rates <0.01% and no timeouts

Attachments included:
- evergreen_rca_summary_20280919.pdf (one-page executive RCA + diagrams)
- evergreen_incident_timeline_091928.csv (detailed event log)
- verification_test_plan_evergreen.xlsx (test steps and pass criteria)

Links:
- Shared RCA folder: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e
- Follow-up ticket: JIRA-REDWOOD-8342
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.example.com/deal/EVB-2028-09

Commercial note: we are preparing a recommended customer goodwill package (usage credit + support hours). I’ll coordinate with our finance team and send a proposed credit range by 2028-09-21. Marissa, can you own the credit proposal?

If you prefer a walk-through, I can set a 30-minute session this week to go through the timeline and test plan.

Best,
Kimberly Park
